title: Thread-safe task scheduler
idea: A thread-safe scheduler lets many worker threads take due tasks from one queue so that each task runs exactly once and idle workers sleep instead of spinning.

analogy.text: A deli counter with a ticket roll. Only one hand pulls a ticket at a time, and staff wait on a bell instead of staring at the queue.
analogy.breaks: A deli bell rings for one customer; signalAll wakes every waiting worker.

points: `PriorityQueue` is not thread-safe; guard every peek and poll with one lock.
Check and poll the head in one locked step, or workers take undue tasks.
Idle workers wait on a `Condition`; submit and clock changes signal them.
Run the job after releasing the lock, so one slow job blocks nobody.

messages.label: takeDue()
messages.note: A takes the lock, finds nothing due, and waits on the condition. Waiting releases the lock.

messages.label: takeDue()
messages.note: B waits the same way. Both workers sleep without burning CPU.

messages.label: submit(T-1)
messages.note: Submit adds the task under the lock, then calls `signalAll`.

messages.label: T-1
messages.note: A wins the lock, re-checks the head, and polls T-1 in the same locked step.

messages.label: nothing due
messages.note: B wakes after A, re-checks, finds an empty head and waits again.

messages.label: takeDue() again
messages.note: A ran the job with the lock released, so others were never blocked by it.

messages.label: cancel(id)
messages.note: Cancel and claim race on one task's status. Compare-and-set lets exactly one win; `DoubleRun` proves it.

code.title: The race, then the fix
code.caption: A barrier forces both workers to check before either acts, so the race shows every time.

walk.text: One task status, a run counter, and a barrier for two threads.
With compare-and-set, the check and the claim are one atomic step.
Without it, check-then-act: both see SCHEDULED, then both claim the task.
Only a thread that claimed the task runs the job.

code.title: Four workers, one locked queue
code.caption: Four workers drain 1,200 tasks. Late tasks wait for the clock, and no task runs twice.

walk.text: Each worker loops: take a due task, run it outside the lock.
1,000 tasks are due at 0; 200 are due at 5000.
Advance the clock and wake workers so they re-check the head.
Submit adds under the lock and signals waiting workers.
Check the head and poll it inside one critical section; otherwise wait.
Shutdown sets a flag and wakes everyone so the loops exit.

pitfalls: Never call the job while holding the queue lock; one slow job freezes every worker.
Always re-check the head in a loop after waking; signals and spurious wakeups lie.
Use compare-and-set for run versus cancel; a plain read then write lets both win.

quiz.q: What does the first line of DoubleRun print?
options: It changes from run to run
quiz.why: The barrier makes both threads read SCHEDULED before either writes RUNNING. Both believe the task is free, so the job runs twice.

takeaway: Claim tasks atomically, wait on a condition, run jobs outside the lock.

starters: Could I use DelayQueue instead of a lock and a condition?
Why signalAll instead of signal when a task is submitted?
How would ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor compare with this design?
